what: glmnet_IBS() rebuilt for start/stop survival data (breaking)
title: TempleCBE 0.2.0
text: Breaking change. glmnet_IBS() now port penalized-Cox tuning code originally meant replace, generalized column names hard-coded. previous version scored plain time/status data IPCW Brier score, treated every start/stop row independent subject, used every numeric column (including identifiers) predictor, returned IBS, lambda, alpha – none fit repeated-measures data. new signature takes rsplit, unprepped recipe (prepped inside fold), feature_names, time_data grid, id_col/start_col/stop_col/status_col, returns IBS, lambda, term, estimate, alpha (one row per coefficient lambda.min), IBS = failure_ibs (default 2) cv.glmnet() fit. censoring_weights = "none" (default) reproduces ported code: interval rows scored censoring weight 1. censoring_weights = "ipcw" scores one row per subject inverse-probability--censoring weights (Graf et al., 1999) analysis-set censoring distribution. two give different numbers; compare within one setting. New tune_over_alpha() summarize_tune_results() tune glmnet_IBS() alpha grid one split every split resample. Neither calls future::plan(). formulas, instead fit one model per candidate feature set, (given randomly drawn) alpha, add formula column. glmnet_IBS() accepts feature_names function baked analysis set, recipes whose output columns vary fold (e.g. step_pca(threshold = )). Bugs fixed relative ported code: alpha grid hard-coded 6 fixed values, produced num_alpha_values + 1 values num_fixed = 6 overwrote fixed values otherwise – now exactly num_alpha_values; outer map splits drew random alpha values workers without seed, grids reproducible – maps now run furrr_options(seed = TRUE); filling missing relative risk looped forever subject known value – now errors naming subject. internal ipcw_brier_score()/integrate_brier_score() helpers old implementation removed; scoring now goes yardstick::brier_survival_integrated().

title: TempleCBE 0.2.0
text: get_model_parameters() returns preprocessor, model, best tuning parameters workflow ranked .rank tuned workflow set results; fit_n_rank() also fits tune::fit_best(). Fixed porting: group_wflow = FALSE, ranked configuration reported workflow’s best configuration fitted; fit used fit_best()’s default metric rather rank_metric. km_summary_to_prism() expands Kaplan-Meier summary--time table GraphPad Prism survival table. Fixed porting: strata_levels documented ignored, validate_totals failed strata_levels set. convert_pdf_to_docx(), convert_pdfs_to_docx(), check_docx_toolchain(), find_python(), find_soffice() convert PDFs DOCX via pdf2docx, LibreOffice, Word COM (Windows), verified backend discovery. convert_pdf_to_docx fits zip_reports(docx_from_pdf = ). Pinned Python requirements ship inst/python/requirements.txt. Interpreters configured options(templecbe.python)/TEMPLECBE_PYTHON options(templecbe.soffice)/TEMPLECBE_SOFFICE. Word COM subprocess now runs calling session’s Rscript rather first one PATH. run_sas_script() runs SAS program batch mode log listing separate folders; find_sas() locates executable (options(templecbe.sas), SAS_EXE, PATH, default install locations). normalize_safely(), parse_here_call_vec(), file_meta_fs(), extract_win_posix_paths(), extract_all_xlsx_tokens() exported: path helpers behind scan_data_io(), code audits file paths . profvis_summary() tabulates profvis profile function: memory, memory increments, call counts, stack depth, memory time. parsnip, profvis, reticulate, tune, workflows, workflowsets, yardstick added Suggests.

title: TempleCBE 0.2.0
text: “Nested Cross-Validation Longitudinal Survival Models” vignette uses new glmnet_IBS() arguments (recipe, feature_names, time_data, id_col) shows censoring weightings; longer built 0.2.0. normalize_safely() returns forward slashes every platform, consistent scan_data_io(). scan_data_io() documents max_depth, zip_render()’s documentation regenerated match code, yaml (used zip_render()) declared Suggests. two R CMD check warnings master. pkgdown reference index lists every exported topic, adding mtry sweeps, render_me(), read_search(), write_search(), scan_data_io(), zip_reports(). Docker image installs libuv1-dev, fs needs load time.

title: TempleCBE 0.1.8
text: missforest_sweep_mtry() sweeps mtry missForest, scores every column --bag error, assembles column whichever run imputed best. missforest_oob_by_mtry() (one fit, tidy per-column OOB table) missforest_impute_by_mtry() (assemble columns winning runs) exported building blocks. consolidates three copies drifted apart analysis code; differences now arguments (exclude identifier/time columns) documented behavior (character--factor coercion inside worker, original column order restored). missranger_sweep_mtry(), missranger_oob_by_mtry(), missranger_max_mtry() run sweep missRanger engine return shape. missranger_max_mtry() computes largest mtry missRanger admits, bounded number complete columns rather ncol - 1. Errors comparable across engines – compare mtry within engine . Bugs fixed relative copies replaces: runs looked position (sweep[[mtry]]), correct grid exactly 1:n; seeding passed future::plan(.options = ...) ignored, sweeps never seeded – seed now reaches furrr::future_map()’s .options; -NA columns, missForest silently drops missRanger silently leaves NA, now refused name. max_pct_missing holds columns missing given share, carries unimputed, reports excluded_high_missing. Defaults NULL (impute everything). Neither sweep calls future::plan(); caller’s backend respected. missForest, missRanger, pkgload added Suggests.

title: TempleCBE 0.1.8
text: columns = "tidy" returns every broom::tidy() column cor.test() (estimate renamed cor), including statistic, degrees freedom, confidence limits. default "compact" output (var1, var2, r, p_value) unchanged. sort chooses "p_value" (default), "estimate", "abs_estimate", "none". ... passed cor.test() (alternative, conf.level, exact). use = "complete.obs" now tests every pair rows. use previously accepted effect tests; unsupported values now error. Behavior change: pairs enumerated column order, var1 column appears first data. Previously whichever name sorted first locale’s collation. Values unchanged; pair’s orientation tie order can differ.

title: TempleCBE 0.1.7
text: Found real render, existing test suite: correlation_plot_split()’s hierarchical clustering, cut fixed k = ceiling(n_vars / group_size), can leave cluster just one variable – confirmed real 7-variable dataset group_size = 6. “group” one variable pairwise correlation show, 1x1 correlation matrix crashes corrplot()’s default order = "FPC" ordering downstream (eigen(corr)$vectors[, 1:2]: subscript bounds – 1x1 matrix’s eigen() second eigenvector index). Added merge_singleton_groups(), internal helper folds singleton cluster whichever group variable correlated average (absolute value), correlation_plot_split() never hands correlation_plot() group one. Verified 15 random variable counts (5-9) errors singleton groups produced. correlation_plot() now errors clearly (“requires least 2 numeric columns”) single-column input, instead failing inside corrplot()’s internals – defense depth direct caller, just calls routed correlation_plot_split().

title: TempleCBE 0.1.6
text: Dockerfile previously ignored committed renv.lock entirely: remotes::install_deps() resolved TempleCBE’s declared DESCRIPTION dependencies whatever versions happened current live CRAN/r-universe build time, exact package versions baked Docker image silently drift renv::restore() installs Windows dev machine pinned lockfile – exactly reproducibility gap renv exists close. image now installs pinned renv (version tracked via new RENV_VERSION build arg, matching existing R_VERSION/QUARTO_VERSION arg convention) runs renv::restore(prompt = FALSE) committed renv.lock, .Rprofile, renv/activate.R/renv/settings.json, Docker builds local renv::restore() Windows now install identical dependency versions. still copied ahead rest source tree (DESCRIPTION previously), restore layer invalidates lockfile changes, every source commit. final package install also switched R CMD INSTALL renv::install("."), since plain R CMD INSTALL doesn’t source .Rprofile can’t see renv-managed library renv::restore() populated – failed find ggplot2/corrplot/etc. even though installed correctly. renv::install() runs inside renv-activated session, avoiding mismatch. (One caveat found verifying built image: renv::status() still reports R’s bundled “recommended” packages – survival, MASS, Matrix, etc. – sync lockfile inside container, renv deliberately avoids overwriting base R installation’s recommended-package versions. expected renv behavior rather gap introduced , doesn’t affect TempleCBE’s dependencies, built image confirmed load run TempleCBE correctly.) renv::snapshot() re-run confirm lockfile current 0.1.5 correlation-plot changes; changes used already-imported packages (stats, ggplot2, corrplot, dplyr, tibble), package versions needed updating – renv.lock unchanged.

title: TempleCBE 0.1.5
text: corrplot() never given top margin, title collided 45-degree diagonal variable-name labels sitting just every rendered plot. Added mar argument (default c(0, 0, 2, 0), standard par("mar") c(bottom, left, top, right) form corrplot() already accepts) title clears labels default, still letting callers override longer titles larger tl.cex. Coefficient numbers hardcoded (addCoef.col = "black") clean way turn . correlation matrix many variables numbers overlap ellipses labels; workaround shrinking tl.cex/number.cex toward zero, doesn’t fix crowding – just deletes every label, leaving unreadable, unlabeled plot. Added show_coef = TRUE argument; setting FALSE omits coefficients cleanly keeping diagonal variable labels intact. default unchanged, existing small-matrix callers see behavior difference.

title: TempleCBE 0.1.5
text: correlation_plot_split(): correlation matrix many variables stay legible one correlation_plot() call (e.g. ~40 clinical parameters), automatically groups variables via hierarchical clustering .dist(1 - abs(cor_mat)) – correlation-based distance corrplot’s order = "hclust" uses – draws one within-group correlation_plot()-style plot per group (default target size 12 variables per group, via ceiling(n_vars / group_size) groups stats::cutree()). sub-plot’s title suffixed "(Group n)" sub-plots can told apart. Returns per-group correlation matrices invisibly, named list, since called (like correlation_plot()) plotting side effect. correlation_diff() / correlation_diff_heatmap(): compare correlation matrix comparison dataset baseline dataset, matching numeric variables column name (falling back intersection two datasets’ numeric columns differ). Unlike pca_loading_diff(), sign-alignment step needed – correlation coefficients, unlike PCA loadings, sign ambiguity. Returns/renders one triangle (symmetric) difference matrix, (always-zero) diagonal dropped. correlation_diff_heatmap() uses diverging, zero-centered fill scale pca_loading_diff_heatmap().

title: TempleCBE 0.1.4
text: pca_biplot(): real PCA loadings biplot. Unlike plot_pca_bi() (draws observation arrow PC score, labeled id column), pca_biplot() draws observation scores muted point cloud overlays variable loading vectors (pca_model$rotation) labeled arrows origin – classic two-panel--one biplot. Loadings rescaled max extent 80% score cloud’s max extent, since raw (unit-scale) loadings otherwise invisible next scores. Works directly fitted prcomp object; newdata argument needed. Added new type = "biplot" option plot.prcomp(). pca_loading_diff(): compares variable loadings two independently-fit prcomp objects variables (e.g. domain baseline vs. later timepoint). Handles PCA’s arbitrary component sign sign-aligning shared component comparison fit baseline differencing, component ’s merely flipped (truly changed) reads ~0 difference instead spurious ~2x jump. Matches variables name falls back intersection two fits’ variable sets differ. pca_loading_diff_heatmap(): renders pca_loading_diff()’s output feature--component heatmap diverging, zero-centered fill scale, matching pca_feature_loading_heatmap()’s visual style.

title: TempleCBE 0.1.4
text: pca_percent_var_explained(): tightened top margin variance bars adding expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.01)) percent--variance y scale.

title: TempleCBE 0.1.3
text: by_column mode now respects row_order argument: row_order = FALSE (default), groups (x-axis) features (y-axis) ordered descending total missingness, matching ordering already applied default per-row/column view. Previously features stayed whatever order pivot_longer() produced (alphabetical), ignoring row_order entirely. by_column mode now auto-detects aggregated missingness effectively binary – .e. every group one contributing row (checked actual group sizes via dplyr::n(), just resulting sums) – case renders discrete “Missing”/“Present” two-level fill “Data Status” legend used default view, instead continuous black--red “# missing” gradient misleading every value 0 1 (e.g. by_column set unique subject/site id one row per group). Groups one contributing row keep existing continuous gradient, since real count meaningful (e.g. multiple readings per site time). Added fill = c("auto", "binary", "count") argument missmap() override auto-detected fill behavior explicitly needed.

title: TempleCBE 0.1.2
text: is_poisson(): chi-squared branch’s distribution.test flag inverted relative every test package (p < 0.1 mislabeled “looks Poisson”), test used statistically invalid cross-tabulation instead real goodness--fit comparison. Replaced proper chi-squared goodness--fit test using quantile-based binning fitted Poisson distribution, degrees freedom correctly reduced estimated rate. Dropped accompanying Kolmogorov-Smirnov test: KS assumes continuous null distribution, Poisson’s real point masses inflate KS statistic regardless true fit. is_normal(): switched comparing freshly simulated random sample (non-deterministic, added unnecessary noise) one-sample KS test fitted normal CDF directly. glmnet_IBS(): per-time-point Brier score normalized sum IPCW weights happened contribute, instead full test-set size — double-counted effect exclusions inflated score. Fixed follow Graf et al. (1999) IPCW estimator exactly; refactored standalone, independently-tested helpers. single_t_test(): paired = TRUE crashed unconditionally (broom::tidy() doesn’t return estimate1/estimate2 paired test) — fold-change now computed directly group vectors. Also added optional .id argument pair observations subject/record identifier instead row order, previously silently mismatched pairs unless two groups pre-sorted identically.

title: TempleCBE 0.1.2
text: ncp never passed FactoMineR::FAMD(), every fit silently capped FactoMineR’s default 5 components regardless num_comp. threshold (cumulative-variance component selection) documented tunable effect; now implemented. options (extra arguments FactoMineR::FAMD()) documented never forwarded; now implemented. print.step_famd() always printed empty column list due incorrect names() call; now uses recipes::print_step() like recipe steps. tidy.step_famd() returned fabricated placeholder values (value = 1.0, component = "PC1" every term) instead real per-component loadings/contributions. bake.step_famd() silently returned data unchanged FactoMineR became unavailable prep(); now errors clear message. Added clear error step_famd() given quantitative qualitative columns (FAMD requires mixed data).

title: TempleCBE 0.1.2
